A massive debris-laden flash flood struck the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha's Chumnubri Rural Municipality after a landslide blocked the river flow. Viral footage captured the shocking moment a giant boulder rolled relentlessly down the grey torrent, highlighting the severe destruction caused by the sudden surge. The flash flood swept away more than 35 houses, several bridges, and local infrastructure across riverside settlements like Jagat and surrounding areas. While authorities have reported no human casualties so far, hundreds of residents have been displaced as rescue teams and security forces mobilize to assess the heavy damage. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and local administration have issued urgent high-risk alerts. Residents along the Budhi Gandaki and Trishuli river corridors have been strictly advised to move away from riverbanks and stay on high ground. For immediate emergency assistance or reporting, contact local disaster management or the Nepal Police hotline at 100 or 112. #GorkhaFlood #BudhigandakiFlood #NepalDisaster #FlashFlood #GorkhaNews

Nepal is once again facing a devastating flood disaster in the Budhigandaki region, causing widespread destruction to hundreds of homes and buildings, damaging major bridges, and disrupting vital road networks connecting key districts. What makes this tragedy even more heartbreaking is that Nepal has barely had time to recover from the recent floods in the Bhotekoshi rasuwa and Trishuli river regions. Now, we are facing yet another disaster, leaving communities displaced, infrastructure damaged, livelihoods destroyed, and countless families living in uncertainty. At this point, we must ask ourselves: How many more disasters must Nepal endure before long-term solutions become a national and international priority? It is true that floods are natural disasters, and no country can completely prevent them. We should not rush to blame any single individual or institution for the forces of nature. However, the scale of destruction, the repeated loss of infrastructure, and the vulnerability of communities raise serious questions about preparedness, disaster-risk management, infrastructure planning, and climate resilience.                                         This is where geopolitics and international cooperation must move beyond diplomatic statements and deliver practical results. Nepal should strengthen regional cooperation with India, China, Bangladesh, and other relevant partners, while using international platforms such as the G20 to advocate for climate finance, disaster-resilient infrastructure, technology transfer, and stronger regional early-warning mechanisms. #prayfornepal #fyp #flood #nepal #budigandaki

Pada Minggu, 11 Oktober 2026, banjir bandang menerjang kawasan Sungai Budhi Gandaki di Distrik Gorkha, Nepal. Air bah membawa lumpur dan menghantam permukiman serta infrastruktur di sejumlah desa. Longsor diduga menyumbat aliran sungai atau anak sungai, kemudian memicu luapan air secara mendadak. Laporan The Kathmandu Post memperkirakan sekitar 35–40 rumah hanyut dan beberapa jembatan rusak atau hancur. Lokasi pembangunan proyek pembangkit listrik tenaga air juga terdampak. Lima orang dilaporkan hilang dalam laporan Reuters, sementara 49 orang berhasil diselamatkan oleh tim militer Nepal. Data korban masih dapat berubah seiring proses pencarian. Sebelumnya pada Rabu, 26 Agustus 2026, banjir bandang dahsyat menerjang Distrik Rasuwa, Nepal, dan berdampak pada sejumlah wilayah di sepanjang aliran Sungai Bhote Koshi dan Trishuli. Laporan awal Radio Nepal pada 26 Agustus mencatat 95 korban meninggal yang telah ditemukan atau terkonfirmasi saat itu. Angka tersebut merupakan data pada tahap awal penanganan bencana. 🚨Shocking visuals coming from Nepal's Gorkha District today. A massive, black debris-filled flood surged down the Budhi Gandaki River early this morning after a landslide blocked the river in Chumnubri village. The temporary dam suddenly burst, unleashing a wall of water, mud and rocks. In the video you can see entire buildings with green roofs being swallowed in seconds as people watch helplessly from the hilltop. According to authorities, more than 35-65 houses in Salleri Bazaar, Jagat, Paiyuka and riverbed settlements have been swept away. At least 4 bridges including 2 motorable bridges were destroyed. 5 to 10 people are reported missing so far, and 49 people have been rescued and airlifted by the Nepal Army. A RED ALERT has been issued for downstream districts - Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi. Residents are being urged to stay away from the river and move to high ground. This comes just 2 months after the deadly August flood in Nepal that killed over 1,400 people. Pray for Nepal. 🙏 #NepalFlood #PrayForNepal #Gorkha #FlashFlood #NepalNews
